title: Git branching: branch, commit, merge
summary: Practise starting a branch, saving work on it, and bringing it back into main.
objective: Create a branch, commit on it, and merge it into main with the right commands in the right order.

hook.prompt: You create a new branch, change `index.html`, and commit. Then you switch back to `main`. What does `index.html` look like on main?

options.text: Just as it was before your change

options.feedback: Your commit lives on the new branch. Main keeps its own version of the file.

options.text: It's gone until you switch back
options.feedback: Main still has the file, in the version main last saved.

hook.explanation: Each branch keeps its own commits, so main doesn't see your change. Let's see how to work on a branch and then bring the change over.

bricks.title: Work on a branch
bricks.body: A **branch** is a separate line of work. **Commits** (saved snapshots of your files) made on it don't change `main`. New commits always land on the branch you're **on**. `git switch -c name` creates a branch and moves you onto it. `git switch name` moves you to a branch that already exists. `git branch name` only creates one: you stay where you are. `git branch` lists branches, with `*` beside yours.

term.definition: A separate line of commits. New commits go to the branch you're on.

visual.code:
git switch -c login-form        # create login-form and move onto it
git branch                      # list branches
#   main
# * login-form
git add .                       # pick the changed files to save
git commit -m "Add login form"  # this commit lands on login-form

bricks.prompt: You're on `main`. Complete the commands to start a `dark-mode` branch and save your work on it.
bricks.template:
git [[a]] -c dark-mode
git add .
git [[b]] -m "Add dark mode"

mistakes.feedback: `git branch` makes a branch but leaves you on main, so your commit would land on main.
`git commit` saves a snapshot. It doesn't create a branch or move you.
`git switch` moves between branches. Saving your work is `git commit`.
`git branch` creates or lists branches. Saving your work is `git commit`.

bricks.hint: One command creates a branch and moves you; another saves a snapshot.
bricks.explanation: `git switch -c dark-mode` creates the branch and moves you onto it, so `git commit` saves your work there.

bricks.prompt: You run `git branch` and see this. Then you commit. Which branch gets the commit?

options.feedback: Main is listed first, but the `*` marks the branch you're on: signup-page.
A commit lands on one branch only: the one you're on.

bricks.explanation: The `*` shows you're on signup-page, and new commits always land on the branch you're on.

bricks.prompt: You're on `signup-page` and want to go back to `main`, which already exists. Which command do you run?

options.feedback: `-c` creates a new branch. Main already exists, so Git refuses to make another.
`git branch name` only creates a branch and never moves you. Main already exists anyway.

bricks.hint: Do you need to create anything, or just move?
bricks.explanation: Main already exists, so you only need to move: `git switch main`, without `-c`.

bricks.prompt: Starting on `main`, you run these commands. Which of the two new commits are on `main`?

visual.code:
git switch -c api
git commit -m "A"
git switch main
git commit -m "B"

options.feedback: A was made while you were on api, so it stays on api.
A landed on api. Main gets B, made after switching back.
B was made after `git switch main`, so it landed on main.

bricks.hint: For each commit, which branch were you on at that moment?
bricks.explanation: A was committed on api. After `git switch main`, B was committed on main. So main has B, and api has A.

bricks.prompt: Sam wanted the fix on its own branch, but the commit landed on `main`. Tap the line that went wrong.

visual.code:
git switch main
git branch header-fix
git add .
git commit -m "Fix header"

bricks.hint: Which line made a branch without moving onto it?
bricks.explanation: `git branch header-fix` created the branch but left Sam on main. `git switch -c header-fix` would have moved Sam onto it.

bricks.title: Merge it back
bricks.body: To **merge** is to bring one branch's commits into another. First switch to the branch that should **receive** the work, then name the branch to bring in. On `main`, `git merge login-form` adds login-form's commits to main; login-form itself doesn't change. Once it's merged, `git branch -d login-form` deletes the finished branch. Its commits stay in main.

term.definition: Bring another branch's commits into the branch you're on.

visual.code:
git switch main            # go to the branch that receives the work
git merge login-form       # bring login-form's commits into main
git branch -d login-form   # delete the finished branch

bricks.prompt: Your `search-bar` branch is finished. Complete the commands to bring it into `main`.

mistakes.feedback: Switch to the branch that receives the work. That's main, not search-bar.
You're already on main. `git merge` names the branch to bring in: search-bar.

bricks.hint: Stand on the receiving branch, then name the one to bring in.
bricks.explanation: On main, `git merge search-bar` brings search-bar's commits into main.

bricks.prompt: You're on `main` and run `git merge pricing`. Which branch gets new commits?

options.feedback: Merging changes the branch you're on. pricing is only read from; it stays the same.
Only the branch you're on receives the commits. pricing stays the same.

bricks.explanation: You're on main, so main receives pricing's commits. pricing itself doesn't change.

bricks.prompt: Starting on `main`, put these steps in order to build a `menu` feature and bring it into main.
bricks.hint: You can only merge from the receiving branch, and only delete a branch once it's merged.
bricks.explanation: Branch off, commit there, return to main, merge menu in, then delete the finished branch.

bricks.prompt: Lee wanted the fix in `main`, but main hasn't changed. Tap the line that went wrong.

visual.code:
git switch -c checkout-fix
git add .
git commit -m "Fix checkout total"
git merge main

bricks.hint: Which branch is Lee on when the merge runs?
bricks.explanation: Lee merged while still on checkout-fix, so main's commits went into checkout-fix. Run `git switch main`, then `git merge checkout-fix`.

challenge.situation: You're halfway through a `profile-page` branch, with your work so far committed. A teammate asks you to fix a typo on `main` right now. The profile page isn't ready to share.

options.text: Switch to main, run `git switch -c typo-fix`, fix and commit, then switch to main and `git merge typo-fix`
options.outcome: Main gets just the typo fix. profile-page waits untouched, and you switch back to it when you're ready.

options.text: Fix the typo on profile-page and commit it there
options.outcome: The fix is saved, but main won't get it until the whole profile page is finished and merged.

options.text: Switch to main, run `git merge profile-page`, then fix the typo
options.outcome: The typo gets fixed, but your half-finished profile page lands in main too.

challenge.hint: Which branch should get the fix, and which work isn't ready for it?
challenge.explanation: A small branch off main keeps the fix separate. Merging only typo-fix gives main exactly the change it needs.

takeaways: Start new work with `git switch -c name`, so your commits land on the new branch.
Check `git branch` for the `*` before you commit: that's where the commit goes.
To merge, switch to the receiving branch first, then `git merge` the other one.
Delete a finished branch with `git branch -d` once it's merged.
